title: Fashion Trends in Kazakhstan
paragraphs: Fashion in Kazakhstan is a fascinating blend of traditional and modern influences. While international brands are popular in cities like Almaty and Astana, there is also a growing movement to celebrate traditional Kazakh designs, patterns, and craftsmanship.

Traditional Kazakh clothing includes the shapan — a long robe worn at ceremonies and celebrations. The takhiya, a traditional hat, and felt boots called sarypyl are also part of the cultural heritage. These items are now being incorporated into modern fashion designs.

Young designers at universities like WKU are creating collections that combine traditional Kazakh patterns (called ornaments) with contemporary cuts and fabrics. Kamila Seitkali visited one such exhibition last spring. 'The colours were stunning — deep reds, golds, and blues. It was a beautiful mix of old and new,' she said.

On the streets of Uralsk, students dress practically. Warm jackets and boots are essential in winter. In spring and summer, bright colours and light fabrics are popular. Many students prefer casual clothes — jeans, hoodies, trainers — but dress smartly for important events.

Fast fashion is a concern among younger generations. Cheap clothes that are worn a few times and then thrown away create enormous amounts of textile waste. In response, many students are choosing to buy second-hand or invest in quality pieces that last longer.

Fashion is not just about appearance — it is a form of expression. What you wear tells a story about who you are, where you come from, and what you value. As Kamila says: 'I love mixing Kazakh-inspired accessories with modern clothes. It's my way of showing who I am.'

dialogue.text: Gulnaz, have you seen those new Kazakh-inspired handbags in the exhibition?

dialogue.text: Yes! They're beautiful but a bit too expensive for me right now.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I know. The quality is excellent though — they're big enough for all my books and sturdy enough.

dialogue.speaker: Gulnaz
dialogue.text: I prefer shopping second-hand. You find amazing things and it's much cheaper.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's a good point. The coat I'm wearing cost only 2,000 tenge — it was second-hand.
